newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Bull trend takes Bucharest bourse prices higher.
newsitem.headline: Bull trend takes Bucharest bourse prices higher.

text.p: The bulk of Bucharest share prices jogged higher again on Thursday in a bull run which has gripped the market since the start of the year fuelled by higher 1996 inflation and a depreciating leu currency.
The uptrend in prices for the sixth consecutive session sent two independent indices to year highs.
Turnover was on the rise, too, gaining 103 million lei to 261.5 million.
"The cross deals introduced today definitely helped to thicken volumes," one trader said.
The stock exchange launched cross deals on Thursday, allowing a broker to act for both the buyer and the seller of a security in the same deal.

Some brokers welcomed the move saying it would boost the pace of trading as well as volumes. Others warned that cross deals, liable to increase liquidity in a first stage, would encourage in-house trading, with brokers piling up shares for future profit-taking and eventually blocking the market.
Traders said the bullish mood was also due to the presence of institutional investors, so far near-absent from the market, and foreign buyers, stuck to the sidelines so far.
But they expected profit-taking to end the rally soon.
The most bullish stock was fertiliser maker Azomures SA, which traded almost half the shares that changed hands on Thursday and took 80 percent of turnover. It closed 1,800 lei stronger at 20,700.
Artrom SA engineering company was also in the focus, trading some 8,000 shares on turnover of 26.6 million lei. The stock put on 300 lei to a 3,350 close.
Two unofficial indices - the VAB and the BIG -- rose by 6.0 and respectively 6.12 percent from the previous session.
